conviction_note: Thin, mostly-priced print: the quarter-side negatives (1Q backlog -23% YoY and Q1 orders -15% on a chassis model change, against an IFIS H1 ordinary consensus of 3.3bn yen, +22% YoY) are in public documents since 7/31 and were shrunk under rule 1, while the positives (Kumamoto-quake recovery demand, new chassis models now out so orders can re-book, policy-share sale gains that management said would lift the dividend) are inference; findings sum to about +0.1 and the scaled number is -0.16 because p_up 47 also carries this name's habit of falling on H1 prints (-2.07% Oct 2024, -2.79% Oct 2025) and a 3.57x margin long, which are reaction history rather than findings - the two disagree in sign by construction and both are near zero.
bar: IFIS consensus (kabuyoho) H1 FY3/27 ordinary profit 3,300m yen, FY ordinary 8,300m (below the company plan of 8,500m, unchanged 4 weeks), https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/report?bcode=6345 ; company gives no H1 profit forecast, only FY plan revenue 63.0bn / OP 7.9bn / ordinary 8.5bn / NI 6.7bn and H1 dividend 33 yen (Q1 tanshin https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260730/140120260729501890.pdf). Consensus is likely one or two analysts, so the bar is single-sourced and sizes on it are capped small.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register: 0.0% (no position >=0.5%), unchanged, as of 2026-10-28 (baseline, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html). Margin ratio 3.57x long (kabutan https://kabutan.jp/stock/?code=6345, 2026-10-29), leveraged retail moderately long. No option skew exists. Run-up -4.5% 20d, -2.96% 5d, and -1.64% this morning to 1,379 before the release (kabutan 09:59 JST). Major holders Itochu ~27-33% and Toyota Industries ~21%, so free float is thin (turnover ~168m yen/day).

findings.finding: Special-vehicle order backlog at 1Q-end was 196 oku yen against 255 a year earlier (-23%), Q1 orders 123 vs 145 (rental 36 vs 58, self-propelled 10 vs 29), which management attributed to customers deferring orders through a chassis model change; that makes the IFIS H1 ordinary consensus of 3.3bn (+22% YoY, implying Q2 ordinary ~2.6bn vs 2.16bn last year) look hard to reach.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 prints with progress below the 5-year average: 2025-10-30 (H1 ordinary -13.5%, 32.6% progress vs 39.6% 5yr) -2.79% next close; 2024-10-25 -2.07% (Yahoo daily bars https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/6345.T?range=3y&interval=1d). Q1 FY3/26 chassis-related miss 2025-07-30: -5.14%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the backlog table has been public since 7/31 and the stock is -4.5% over 20 days. What is not visibly priced is the gap to the H1 consensus: IFIS still carries 3.3bn H1 ordinary, unchanged over four weeks; if the street had marked H1 down for the backlog the consensus H1 would sit near last year's 2.7bn. The release is not expected to ADD a forecast cut (no H1 revision in the last three years), so per rule 1 this is sized small.
findings.independence: Same company, different document: the 8/3 presentation Q&A (A7) confirms the order decline and its chassis cause, https://www.aichi-corp.co.jp/hubfs/aichi-corp.co.jp/files/news/2026/09/2026_1_presentation.pdf ; consensus from https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/report?bcode=6345. Both rest on company disclosure.

findings.finding: Q1 operating-profit bridge showed raw-material inflation -1.6 oku yen against price revisions +0.9 and an inventory write-down in special vehicles (segment gross profit -38%), and management said power-utility pricing is set mid-year so pass-through lags, pointing to margin pressure continuing into Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separable record of a margin-only surprise; Q1 FY3/27 (OP margin 3.3%, write-down disclosed) moved +0.76% on 2026-07-31.
findings.why_not_priced: Public in the Q1 deck; the market looked through it at Q1 (+0.76%). The only unpriced part is whether it persisted into the seasonally larger Q2, where last year's OP margin was 13.0%; a Q2 margin below ~12% would show it. Sized small because it is a continuation of a known line.
findings.independence: Shares the company as source with finding 1 but is a different line (margin, not volume); Q1 tanshin segment text confirms the write-down, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260730/140120260729501890.pdf (same issuer).

findings.finding: Two Q2 order tailwinds the 1Q backlog does not show: the 2026-07-28 Kumamoto earthquake (company pledged recovery vehicles and service support for power and telecom customers) and management's statement that both main chassis makers' new models are now out so deferred orders can be booked; the Q2 order and backlog table published with the results can show a rebound.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders tables are released with or a day after the tanshin; FY3/27 Q1 orders fell 15% and the stock rose 0.76%, so the order line has not moved this name much alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing quantifies Q2 orders before the release and the stock has drifted down 4.5% in 20 days and 1.6% this morning, which is not what a priced order rebound looks like. It is an inference from management statements, so sized small.
findings.independence: none (management's own statements in one deck)

findings.finding: Management said gains from selling policy shareholdings (cut from about 8% to a 6% target, Q1 already booked a 273m yen investment-securities gain) will be added to the dividend base at the 60%+ payout, so an H1 print with further sale gains can carry a net-profit or dividend increase above the planned 65 yen.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY3/26 results with a 5-yen dividend raise to 65: +5.65% on 2026-04-27; no H1 dividend change in the last three H1 prints (H1 dividend held each time).
findings.why_not_priced: No 特別利益 notice has been filed on TDnet since Q1 (checked lists 10/27-10/29 and kabutan news), so any Q2 sale gain is unseen; a 4.7% yield name trading flat-to-down into the print is not pricing a dividend bump. Probability of an actual revision at H1 is low, hence the small centre with a fat right tail.
findings.independence: Q1 tanshin cash-flow note records the 273m yen gain, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260730/140120260729501890.pdf (same issuer, different document).

outside_window.finding: Itochu raised its holding from 23.61% to 32.88% (obligation date 2026-04-07) and Toyota Industries still holds about 21%; any further restructuring of the two-parent register (a full takeover or a Toyota Industries exit) has no dated catalyst inside the window.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: unlikely (no H1 revision in three years, plan held at Q1, IFIS FY 8.3bn already below plan 8.5bn so a held plan is mild relief). Returns: H1 dividend 33 planned; a bump only if policy-share gains are booked and NI forecast lifted, low probability. New-year guide: not applicable (H1). Quarter: H1 ordinary progress was 40.9%/38.0%/32.6% in FY3/24-26; my read of ~2.8-3.0bn H1 ordinary is ~33-35% of 8.5bn, below the 5-year average and below IFIS 3.3bn.

rejected_candidates.detail: Measured on the actual TDnet/kabutan release dates the last 11 reactions have a median absolute move of 2.07% (Yahoo bars); the estimated-cadence dates caught non-event moves. Used for scale only, not a finding.

rejected_candidates.detail: Management stated the recall's impact on this year's results is minor; no figure to size.

baseline_tension: priced_lean is -0.05 and the run-up -4.5%, with the stock -1.6% this morning, so the tape already leans the way the quarter-side findings point; the strongest positives the release could carry are a held FY plan above consensus, a Q2 orders rebound after the chassis change and the Kumamoto quake, and a dividend lift from policy-share gains, all three looked for and none confirmable before the print, which is why the net is near zero.
lessons_applied: Rule 1: the backlog/progress negative rests on the public 7/31 order table and a progress rate anyone can compute, and the release is not expected to add a forecast cut, so finding 1 went from -0.8 to -0.5 and p_up from 45 to 47.
Rule 1: the margin-pressure finding rests on the same public Q1 deck, so it went from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 2: wrote the strongest positives into baseline_tension; I had already searched for them (orders rebound, dividend from share-sale gains, held plan), so p_up moved only once, under rule 1.
